output.answer: Yes. The most recent report I found, dated August 11, 2026, says LinkedIn is shutting down its Israeli R&D operation and laying off nearly all of its roughly 50 employees; LinkedIn confirmed proposed organizational changes but did not state an exact number. Earlier, on May 13, LinkedIn confirmed broader organizational changes affecting teams including engineering, product, marketing and its Global Business Organization; Reuters reported the reduction as about 5% of staff, but that percentage was not confirmed by LinkedIn.
caveats: The August report describes proposed organizational changes and says nearly all of the approximately 50-person Israeli center would be affected, but it does not give a final confirmed layoff count.
The often-cited May estimate of about 5% (roughly 875 roles) was reported by Reuters from sources and should not be treated as a headcount officially confirmed by LinkedIn.
This answer reflects information publicly available through November 11, 2026; the sources opened did not establish whether additional unreported cuts occurred after August.

key_facts.fact: LinkedIn was reported on August 11, 2026 to be ending its Israeli R&D operations and laying off nearly all employees there; the center employed about 50 people, with a small number expected to remain temporarily.
A LinkedIn spokesperson confirmed proposed organizational changes in response to the Israel report, but did not provide an exact layoff count.
LinkedIn confirmed organizational changes on May 13, 2026, while reporting identified affected areas including the Global Business Organization, marketing, engineering and product.

Reuters reported that the May 2026 global reduction was about 5% of LinkedIn's staff, based on sources familiar with the matter; LinkedIn did not publicly confirm that percentage in the opened sources.
